subject.title: fix(mcp): honor `disabled` flag to prevent spawning disabled servers

question: Should `disabled` become a supported public MCP configuration alias, or should OpenClaw retain `enabled` as the sole runtime setting and handle legacy input only through doctor migration?
rationale: This PR changes the durable MCP configuration contract, including behavior for hand-edited and conflicting configuration, which cannot be safely chosen by an automated repair.

options.title: Keep one canonical setting
options.body: Retain `enabled` as the only supported runtime/config schema field and repair any legacy `disabled` shape through the MCP doctor migration path.

options.title: Support the alias deliberately
options.body: Document `disabled`, define its precedence when both fields appear, normalize both boolean values on reads and writes, and add fresh-install plus upgrade coverage.

recommendation.title: Keep one canonical setting
recommendation.body: Retain `enabled` as the only supported runtime/config schema field and repair any legacy `disabled` shape through the MCP doctor migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged MCP doctor work is the strongest available adjacent ownership signal for the migration and probe boundary.
